name: Question 1
problem:
$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2x, & x\in [-3,0) \\ {x}^{2}, & x\in [0,3)\end{aligned}
$$

The above function $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [-3,3).$ Let $f(x)$ be the $6$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in R.$
Select the correct options below.

| I. | $F(x)$ is continuous on $x\in (-3,3)$ | {{field-1}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| II. | $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-3,3)$ | {{field-2}} |
| III. | ${lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}F(x)$ | {{field-3}} |
| IV. | $f(x)$ is piecewise smooth and continuous on $R$ | {{field-4}} |
worked_solution:
Let's examine the given statements in turn.

- Statement I is $\text{true}.$ The function $F(x)$ is continuous on $x\in (-3,3).$ Its graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14128659/assets/11f9718c9384ad2fea0bf3f5cc7da720559c512a5b3cebbc11ca966d5ec0f28b.png)

- Statement II is $\text{true}.$ The function $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-3,3).$ It consists of two smooth pieces.

- Statement III is $\text{false}.$ Indeed, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}2x=2(-3)=-6
$$

and 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}{x}^{2}=(3)^{2}=9.
$$

So, ${lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}F(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}F(x).$

- Statement IV is $\text{false}$ since statement III is false.

**Note:** The $6$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in R$ has the graph shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14128659/assets/d0212ece76aba288e88b0c4d9f2e0f6163f4fd1f594cee30e9ea5f764ebc5f69.png)
